solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Check question in material with a pattern

parts.note: to dam is to check or hold back a flow
to question someone is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone checking whether a patterned fabric is the right one.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a reversible woven fabric, often silk or linen, with a figured design.

clue.text: State legislation defended by special envoy, at first

indicators.note: the law is guarded on both sides, so it sits inside

parts.note: dear can mean special, precious
law is legislation

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of envoy

explanation.surface: A new law protected by a special envoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaware is a state of the USA, the first to ratify the Constitution.

clue.text: Error: I am going the wrong way before race

indicators.note: the first piece is placed ahead of the second
means the contraction is read backwards

parts.note: contracted to I'm
a sprint is a short race

explanation.surface: A runner admitting a mistake: heading off the wrong way before a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going the wrong way' turns IM into MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A misprint is a printing mistake, a typo.

clue.text: Very wet prune eaten by mole

indicators.note: the spy swallows the pruning word, so it sits inside

parts.note: a mole is a spy inside an organisation
to lop is to cut off branches, prune

explanation.surface: A soggy dried plum devoured by a burrowing mole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prune' looks like the fruit; it is the verb meaning cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy ground or food is wet and slushy.

clue.text: Red ace for example last, not first

parts.note: an ace is one example of a playing card

indicators.note: says the opening letter of the word for last is dropped

parts.note: the last one is the final one

explanation.surface: A card player hoping the red ace turns up as the final card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not first' takes F off FINAL, leaving INAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal is a deep scarlet colour, named after the robes worn by Catholic cardinals.

clue.text: We don't know who wrote that body of work: initial unseen

definitions.text: We don't know who wrote that

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is not shown

parts.note: an author's canon is their body of work

explanation.surface: A scholar admitting the author of a body of work is unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon, short for anonymous, is printed under a text whose author is unidentified.

clue.text: Outspoken individual being diplomatic

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: discrete means separate, individual

explanation.surface: A blunt person somehow managing to be tactful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outspoken' looks like a description of a person; it signals the sound. DISCRETE and DISCREET sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Being discreet means tactful and careful not to embarrass others.

clue.text: 4 more insensitive?

explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as NUMB+ER means more numb; 4 across, CARDINAL, is a counting number.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are the counting figures one, two, three; numb means without feeling.

clue.text: Winger setting up comprehensive victory?

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: ten-nil is a thrashing score

explanation.surface: A football winger creating a crushing win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' looks like a footballer; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A linnet is a small finch, and birds are 'wingers' in crosswords.

clue.text: More flesh exposed, period!

definitions.meaning: read cryptically as the answer: wearing fewer clothes shows more skin
a period in a school timetable

explanation.surface: An exclamation about someone showing more skin, full stop.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a pun: split the answer as LESS ON, i.e. fewer clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: A school day is divided into periods, each one a class or teaching session.

clue.text: Knight — or centaur?

definitions.meaning: a knight is a mounted soldier, a rider
a centaur is literally half horse, half man

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into HORSE and MAN, which is just what a centaur is.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight fought on horseback, so he is a rider; the mythical centaur joins a horse body to a human torso.

clue.text: Australian native has party set up in street

indicators.note: places the reversed party inside the street

parts.note: way, as in a street name

indicators.note: in a down clue, reads the word upwards

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: An Aussie local throwing a street party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses BALL to LLAB.
explanation.definitionFit: The wallaby is a marsupial native to Australia, a small kangaroo relative.

clue.text: Baffling case of woeful parody — art of the crossword?

indicators.note: something baffling is confused, so the letters are jumbled
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written as part of the letters to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A critic dismissing a clumsy spoof as the sort of thing crossword setters do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' gives WL, the outside letters of woeful; with PARODY that is shuffled by 'Baffling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic clues rely on puns, anagrams and other tricks with language, the craft behind every clue.

clue.text: Picnic in fresh air?

definitions.meaning: informally, a picnic is an easy task, as in 'no picnic'
a fresh breath of air is a light wind

explanation.walkthrough: 'Picnic' looks like an outdoor meal; it is the informal sense of something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy task is called a doddle or cinch; a gentle wind outdoors is also this word.

clue.text: Top cricketer

definitions.meaning: a cricket bowler who spins the ball

explanation.walkthrough: 'Top cricketer' reads as 'best player'; it is two senses side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's spinning toy is a spinner, and so is a slow bowler who turns the ball in cricket.

clue.text: Disgusting position

explanation.definitionFit: Rank describes something foul or rotten; separately, a rank is someone's standing in an army or hierarchy.

clue.text: One about to fall for shoe?

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a made-up literal one: a person who slips.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipper is light footwear worn around the house.

clue.text: Animal stroked, soft touch

definitions.meaning: a pet cat, stroked and fussed

explanation.definitionFit: A pet cat is often petted; informally, a mild, gentle person is called a pussycat.

clue.text: Jam ultimately in fashion with a light meal

indicators.note: places that letter inside the verb

parts.note: to fashion something is to create it

indicators.note: picks the final letter of Jam

explanation.surface: Fashionable jam, served at a light meal.
explanation.walkthrough: A cream tea is a British afternoon snack of tea with scones, jam and clotted cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea is a small afternoon spread, a snack rather than a full meal.

clue.text: Set off into morning 13, for example?

indicators.note: places the jumbled letters inside

parts.note: early in the day, so early

indicators.note: set off means the letters are moved out of order

explanation.surface: Setting off early, perhaps in a breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SET to STE, which goes into EARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: 13 across is BREEZE; an easterly is a wind blowing from the east.

clue.text: Worker guzzling port, union man?

indicators.note: the worker swallows the port, so it goes inside

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
USB is a computer port for plugging in devices

explanation.surface: A labourer drinking port, who also belongs to a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine but is a computer socket; 'union' is marriage, not a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage is a union, and the man in it is the husband.

clue.text: Song somewhat vulgar, I assert

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone declaring a song to be rather crude.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera or oratorio.

clue.text: Couple of those full of beans, perhaps, in dance

indicators.note: a couple means two, so the tin word is written twice in a row

parts.note: tins of beans are cans

explanation.surface: Two lively people out dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of beans' looks like lively people; it is tins, and 'Couple of' gives two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a high-kicking French music-hall dance.

clue.text: Feline drinking Beaujolais, emotional!

indicators.note: the cat swallows the wine, so it goes inside

parts.note: mog is British slang for a cat
Beaujolais is French wine, vin in French

explanation.surface: A cat lapping French wine, getting tearful.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving means stirring the emotions, touching.

clue.text: American rodent, one overcome by a disease

indicators.note: in a down clue, the one sits beneath the rest

parts.note: gout is a joint disease
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An American rodent struck down by an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: The agouti is a South and Central American burrowing rodent.

clue.text: Turn on a device filled with oxygen

indicators.note: the trick has the oxygen symbol put inside it

parts.note: a device can be a trick or stratagem, a ruse
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Switching on a gadget that is pumped full of oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'device' looks like a gadget; it is a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn someone on is to excite or stimulate them.

clue.text: Reading dreadful script in the end, fading star

indicators.note: something dreadful is a mess, so the letters are jumbled
points to the closing letter of script

explanation.surface: A washed-up actor giving an awful reading of a script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fading star' suggests a has-been actor, but it is the astronomical object.
explanation.definitionFit: A red giant is a large, cool star late in its life, near the end of burning its fuel.

clue.text: Capital of Vietnam I looked up

indicators.note: in a down clue, the letters are read upwards
a run of letters taken out of the next words

explanation.surface: Someone who looked up the capital of Vietnam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Vietnam' wants Hanoi; the capital is in Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru.

clue.text: Doubled-up feature down the hatch

indicators.note: doubled up says the facial feature is written twice in a row

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A double chin, perhaps from too much drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubled-up' gives the facial feature twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal toasts, like cheers, said as glasses are raised.

clue.text: Piano perfect for club

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
perfect as in complete, utter

explanation.surface: A piano described as ideal for a music club.
explanation.definitionFit: A putter is the golf club used on the green to roll the ball into the hole.

clue.text: Thing flying ahead of vessel, bird

indicators.note: the first part comes before the second
letters sent flying are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: a jar is a container, a vessel

explanation.surface: Something airborne in front of a ship, which turns out to be a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightjar is a nocturnal insect-eating bird with a churring call.

clue.text: Criminal activity, good and titillating

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, so good
racy means risqué, titillating

explanation.surface: Something illegal that is both virtuous and exciting, a paradox.
explanation.definitionFit: Piracy is robbery at sea, or illegal copying of material.
